questions.text: Do you use AI systems in your service or internal operations?
For each AI system: purpose, provider or model, whether personal data enters prompts or logs, hosting region.
Is customer data used to train or fine-tune any model (yours or the provider's)?
Is AI output reviewed by a human before it affects a person or a customer?
Do staff receive training on AI use (AI literacy)? Describe, or answer none.
Do users interact directly with an AI system (chatbot, voice agent)? If yes, are they told?
Does any system generate synthetic audio, image, video or text published to others?
Are AI outputs used for decisions about employees, applicants, credit, insurance, education or access to essential services?
Does any system infer emotions or sentiment of people (customers, callers, employees)?
Do you maintain an inventory of AI systems and owners?

flags.trigger: Q9 = yes AND the people include employees or students (workplace or education)
flags.text: Inferring emotions of people in the workplace or in education institutions is prohibited under the EU AI Act, except for medical or safety reasons (Art. 5(1)(f)). This may apply. Obtain qualified advice before continuing.

flags.trigger: Q9 = yes AND the people are not employees or students
flags.text: Emotion inference has specific rules (transparency, possible high-risk classification). Obtain qualified advice.
Uses in these areas may be classified as high-risk (Annex III). Obligations depend on role and dates. Obtain qualified advice.
Users interacting with an AI system generally must be informed that they are (Art. 50).
Under Art. 4, providers and deployers of AI systems must take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff.
